author: verrerie
body:
## Phase 1b: Database Infrastructure

Complete database setup for portfolio management.

### 🗄️ Database Setup
- **MariaDB 11.8** via Docker Compose
- Comprehensive schema with 9 tables
- 2 views for common queries
- 1 stored procedure for atomic transactions
- Seed data with example portfolio and tags
- Migration system ready

### 📊 Schema Design

**Core Tables:**
- `portfolios` - Portfolio metadata
- `holdings` - Current positions with average cost
- `transactions` - Complete transaction history
- `watchlists` - Research candidates
- `investment_theses` - Investment reasoning and theses
- `portfolio_snapshots` - Daily performance tracking
- `tags` - Categorization system
- `holding_tags` - Many-to-many tags
- `schema_migrations` - Version control

**Features:**
- UUID primary keys
- Foreign key constraints
- Indexes for performance
- Check constraints for data validation
- Audit timestamps
- Stored procedure: `add_transaction` (atomic updates)

### 📚 Documentation
- `docs/DATABASE.md` - Complete setup and management guide
- `database/README.md` - Quick reference and migrations
- `env.example` - Environment configuration template

### 🧪 Tested
- ✅ Database starts successfully
- ✅ All tables created
- ✅ Seed data loaded (19 tags, 5 watchlist items, 1 portfolio)
- ✅ Healthcheck passes
- ✅ Commands verified

### 📦 What's Included
- Docker Compose configuration
- Initialization scripts (schema + seed data)
- Migration framework
- Comprehensive documentation
- Updated README with database setup

### 🎯 Next Steps
After merge:
- Build Portfolio MCP Server
- Implement core portfolio tools
- Add learning features

### ⚠️ Breaking Change
Requires Docker and Docker Compose to be installed.

---

**Ready for review!** All database infrastructure is in place for Phase 1b Portfolio Management.

author: romanrnlt
body:
## Summary

This release includes automatic versioning workflow, comprehensive security headers, and workflow permission fixes.

## Changes Included

### 1. Automatic Versioning Workflow (#22)

Added GitHub Actions workflow for automatic version bumping based on PR labels.

**Features:**
- ✅ Automatic version bump when merging to main
- ✅ Based on PR labels: `release:major`, `release:minor`, `release:patch`
- ✅ Creates git tags and GitHub releases
- ✅ Follows Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0)
- ✅ Git hook reminder before pushing to main

**Usage:**
- Add `release:patch` label for bugfixes (1.0.3 → 1.0.4)
- Add `release:minor` label for new features (1.0.3 → 1.1.0)
- Add `release:major` label for breaking changes (1.0.3 → 2.0.0)

### 2. Nginx Security Headers (#23)

Added comprehensive security headers to nginx configuration.

**Security Headers:**
- ✅ X-Frame-Options: DENY (prevents clickjacking)
- ✅ X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (prevents MIME sniffing)
- ✅ X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block (XSS protection)
- ✅ Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (privacy)
- ✅ Permissions-Policy (restricts camera, microphone, geolocation)
- ✅ Content-Security-Policy (strict CSP with analytics/errors whitelist)
- ✅ server_tokens off (hides nginx version)

**OWASP Category:** A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration  
**Expected Score:** A+ on securityheaders.com

### 3. Workflow Permissions Fix (#25)

Fixed GitHub Actions permission error for version bumping.

**Changes:**
- ✅ Added `contents: write` permission to workflows
- ✅ Added `pull-requests: read` permission
- ✅ Added `persist-credentials: true` to checkout

**Error Fixed:**
```
Permission to RnltLabs/rnltlabs.git denied to github-actions[bot]
fatal: unable to access [...]: 403
```

## Version Bump

This PR has the `release:minor` label and will trigger:
- **Current version:** v1.1.0
- **New version:** v1.2.0
- Git tag `v1.2.0` will be created
- GitHub Release will be published

## Test Plan

- [x] Auto-versioning workflow files created
- [x] Security headers added to nginx.conf
- [x] Workflow permissions fixed
- [x] All changes merged to develop
- [ ] Merge to main triggers version bump (v1.1.0 → v1.2.0)
- [ ] Verify git tag v1.2.0 is created
- [ ] Verify GitHub Release is published
- [ ] Verify security headers after deployment
- [ ] Test securityheaders.com score (expect A+)
- [ ] Verify Umami Analytics still works
- [ ] Verify GlitchTip error tracking still works

## Breaking Changes

None - this is a backwards-compatible minor release.

## Documentation

- `VERSIONING.md` - Automatic versioning guide
- `NGINX_SECURITY_HEADERS.md` - Security headers documentation

## References

- OWASP Secure Headers: https://owasp.org/www-project-secure-headers/
- Semantic Versioning: https://semver.org/
- GitHub Actions Permissions: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication

---

**Note:** This PR has the `release:minor` label, so version will bump to **v1.2.0** upon merge.

author: konard
body:
## Summary

This PR formalizes Daegene Song's 2014 P≠NP attempt from the paper "The P versus NP Problem in Quantum Physics" (arXiv:1402.6970) and demonstrates why it fails to establish P ≠ NP.

## Implementation Details

### Paper Analysis

The paper claims to prove P ≠ NP by:
1. Interpreting P as deterministic polynomial-time physical processes
2. Interpreting NP as nondeterministic polynomial-time physical processes  
3. Exhibiting a quantum self-reference phenomenon (process "P2") that supposedly belongs to NP \ P

The main argument involves observing the evolution of a quantum reference frame with respect to itself, claiming this creates nondeterminism between the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures.

### Critical Errors Identified

1. **Picture Equivalence**: The Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures are mathematically equivalent and always yield identical physical predictions (expectation values)

2. **No Decision Problem**: Process P2 is not a valid decision problem - it lacks an input, output, and decidable property

3. **Misunderstanding Nondeterminism**: The "choice" between quantum mechanical pictures is a choice of mathematical representation, not computational nondeterminism in the complexity theory sense

4. **Invalid Argument Structure**: Even if the premises were true, the conclusion doesn't follow - physical processes don't directly correspond to complexity classes

### Formalization

Created formalizations in three proof assistants:

- **Coq** (`coq/DaegeneSong2014.v`): 450+ lines formalizing the argument and proving the errors
- **Lean** (`lean/DaegeneSong2014.lean`): 300+ lines with type-safe refutation
- **Isabelle** (`isabelle/DaegeneSong2014.thy`): 280+ lines demonstrating the flaws

All formalizations:
- Define the quantum mechanical framework (simplified)
- Formalize Song's process P2 and the claimed nondeterminism
- Prove that the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures yield identical predictions
- Show that P2 cannot be formalized as a decision problem
- Demonstrate the confusion between different conceptual levels

### Documentation

Comprehensive README.md includes:
- Full description of the attempt and main argument
- Detailed analysis of each error
- References to the paper and related work
- Educational value explaining common P vs NP proof pitfalls

## Testing

- ✅ Lean formalization compiles successfully (with expected `sorry` placeholders)
- ⏳ Coq and Isabelle will be tested by CI (tools not available locally)

## Fixes

Fixes #315

---

*This PR was created as part of the systematic effort to formalize P vs NP proof attempts from Woeginger's list*

Continued AI/ML security implementation per `docs/copilot/ai_ml.md`. Fixed 6 detection failures and implemented context-aware detection to reduce false positives.

## Detection Fixes (6/6 complete)

**AIML506**: Added `_check_dp_parameter_assignment()` to detect hardcoded privacy budgets in assignments, not just function calls.

**AIML499**: Enhanced pattern matching to recognize gradient aggregation (`aggregate_gradients(client_gradients)`) without explicit "federated" keywords.

**AIML503**: Added library-specific detection for `seal.encrypt`, `pyfhel`, `tenseal` HE libraries.

**AIML504**: Changed from federated-learning-only to direct TEE/enclave usage detection with attestation validation.

**AIML505**: Detects split learning via client/server model forwarding patterns (`client_model.forward()` → `server_model.forward(activations)`).

**AIML509**: Recognizes encryption + inference patterns (`he_encrypt` + `model.predict`) with key management validation.

## Context-Aware Detection

Implemented `_check_context_for_keywords()` to check ±3 lines for validation patterns, eliminating false positives when safety checks occur on adjacent lines:

```python
# Previously flagged as vulnerable
story = model.generate("Write a story")
verified_story = copyright_check(story)  # Now detected as safe

# Detection checks surrounding context
has_check = (
    any(x in line_text for x in ["copyright", "license"]) or
    self._check_context_for_keywords(node.lineno, ["copyright_check", "license"])
)
```

Applied to AIML464 (copyright infringement). Pattern documented for remaining 14 false positives.

- **510 AIML checks** implemented (102% of 500 target)
- **Test pass rate**: 91.3% → 94.2% (260/276 passing)
- **Detection rate**: 100% (6/6 failures fixed)

body:
After creating a new task, the back button on the task detail screen was non-functional, requiring users to close and reopen the app to navigate away.

## Root Cause

Navigation logic always popped the backstack twice regardless of context:
- **Create mode**: Stack is `[Previous] → [TaskEdit]` — needs 1 pop
- **Edit mode**: Stack is `[Previous] → [TaskDetail] → [TaskEdit]` — needs 2 pops

Popping twice in create mode removed the entire backstack, leaving nothing to navigate to.

## Changes

### TaskEditViewModel
- Added `isCreateMode` boolean to `NavigateToDetail` event
- Captured flag locally before async save to prevent state mutation issues

### TaskEditScreen
- Updated navigation callback signature: `(String) → Unit` to `(String, Boolean) → Unit`

### LifeOpsNavGraph
- Conditional backstack popping based on `isCreateMode`:

```kotlin
onNavigateToTaskDetail = { taskId, isCreateMode ->
    if (isCreateMode) {
        navController.popBackStack()  // Pop TaskEdit only
    } else {
        navController.popBackStack()  // Pop TaskEdit
        navController.popBackStack()  // Pop old TaskDetail
    }
    navController.navigate(Screen.TaskDetail.createRoute(taskId))
}
```

Fixes issue where back navigation was broken after creating tasks from Today or All Tasks screens.

  - Type-3: Regular languages → finite automata → lexical analysis

body:
## Description
This PR introduces a scheduled job to automatically create and submit accounting document proposals to MISA for both **QR** and **Manual** payments.

### Key Changes
* **Scheduled Voucher Creation**
  * Introduces a new **MisaVoucherCreator** service responsible for the entire voucher creation workflow.
  * Adds new cron triggers in `wrangler.jsonc` to run the job at **08:30**, **13:30**, and **18:00** (local time).
  * Updates `schedule-handler.js` to route these cron jobs to the corresponding methods in the new service.

* **Handling MISA’s  Queue-based API**
  * Because MISA’s API processes voucher submissions asynchronously, a unique org_refid (GUID) is generated locally for each voucher and saved back to its payment record using a Prisma `$transaction` after successfully sending the payload to MISA.
  * Note: MISA does not return detailed error messages in their “Save Voucher” API.  
    Instead, a successful response looks like this:
    ```json
    {
        "Success": true,
        "ErrorMessage": "",
        "Data": "Hệ thống đã ghi nhận yêu cầu đồng bộ vào hàng đợi, dữ liệu sẽ được đồng bộ sang hệ thống AMIS Kế toán sớm nhất có thể. Sau khi xử lý xong yêu cầu đồng bộ, hệ thống sẽ trả kết quả đồng bộ vào đường dẫn callback mà đối tác đã cung cấp cho AMIS kế toán."
    }
    ```

A future PR will handle MISA’s callback response to update each payment’s `misa_synced` status once the voucher has been successfully processed.

body:
Previous PowerShell script failed when building the professor service Docker image from the root directory due to attempting `cd` into a duplicate/non-existent path.

## Changes

### Created `setup-dev-env.ps1`
Complete automation script (385 lines) that:
- Verifies prerequisites (Docker, Minikube, kubectl)
- Starts Minikube if not running (`minikube start` with resource allocation)
- Configures Docker environment (`minikube docker-env | Invoke-Expression`)
- Builds all Docker images with corrected path handling
- Applies K8s manifests in order: infrastructure (PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ) → backend services → frontend
- Provides colored output and final access instructions

### Path Handling Fix
The critical fix checks if already in target directory before attempting navigation:

```powershell
function Build-DockerImage {
    param([string]$FolderPath, ...)
    
    # Only cd if not already in target directory
    if ($FolderPath -ne ".") {
        Set-Location $FolderPath
    }
    
    docker build -t $ImageTag .
    
    # Return to root if we changed directories
    if ($FolderPath -ne ".") {
        Set-Location $rootDir
    }
}

# Professor Service builds from root without erroneous cd
Build-DockerImage -FolderPath "." -ImageTag "distrischool-professor-tecadm-service:latest"
```

- `TESTING_MINIKUBE.md`: Added automated setup section at top, promoted section 11 to "Recomendado"

body:
Implements a complete PHP task management application with JSON-based persistence, CSRF protection, and responsive UI per project requirements.

## Implementation

**Backend modules (`src/`):**
- `storage.php` - JSON CRUD operations, secure ID generation via `random_bytes()`
- `validation.php` - Server-side validation (title required ≤255 chars, description ≤1000 chars)
- `csrf.php` - Token generation/validation using cryptographically secure random bytes
- `flash.php` - Session-based one-time messaging

**Frontend (`public/`):**
- `index.php` - Task list sorted by completion status, then priority (High→Medium→Low)
- `create.php` - Task creation form with validation and error display
- `actions.php` - POST handler for create/delete/toggle operations, returns HTTP 405 for non-POST

**Styling:**
- Fully responsive CSS with breakpoints at 768px and 480px
- Priority color coding (High: red, Medium: orange, Low: blue)
- Mobile-optimized stacked layout

## Security

- CSRF tokens on all forms using `hash_equals()` for timing-attack resistance
- XSS prevention via `htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8')` on all output
- Task IDs use 32-char hex strings from `random_bytes(16)` instead of predictable `uniqid()`
- HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for non-POST requests to action handler

## Example Usage

```php
// Create task with validation
$validation = validateTask($_POST);
if ($validation['valid']) {
    $task = sanitizeTask($_POST);
    addTask($task);
}

// Task structure
[
    'id' => 'task_a3b2c1...', // 32-char secure random hex
    'title' => 'Complete project',
    'priority' => 'high',
    'completed' => false,
    'created_at' => '2025-10-26 23:35:56'
]
```

- Added Scala 3.3.4 to `crossScalaVersions` for all modules (bytes, crypto, rlp, node)
- Separated version-specific compiler options: `scala2Options` for `-Ywarn-unused`, `-Xlint`; `scala3Options` for `-Ykind-projector`
- Dynamic `scalacOptions` selection based on `CrossVersion.partialVersion(scalaVersion.value)`

- **Scalafmt**: 2.7.5 → 3.8.3 with `runner.dialect = scala213source3` for gradual migration
- **sbt-scalafmt**: 2.4.2 → 2.5.2
- **scala3-migrate**: 0.6.1 plugin added for migration analysis

## CI Pipeline
- Matrix build strategy: `scala-version: ['2.13', '3.3']`
- Scapegoat excluded from Scala 3 builds (not yet compatible)
- Version-tagged artifacts: `coverage-reports-jdk17-scala-${{ matrix.scala-version }}`

## Migration Commands
```bash
sbt scala3Migrate           # Run migration analysis
sbt scala3MigrateSyntax     # Syntax compatibility check
sbt compileScala3           # Compile with ++3.3.4
sbt testScala3              # Test with ++3.3.4
```

Switch to a Map of TransactionEventFilter by Address to better avoid excessive comparisons

### Checklist

* [x] I wrote new tests for my new core changes.
* [x] I have successfully ran tests, style checker and build against my new changes locally.
* [x] I have informed the team of any breaking changes if there are any.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Replaces flat event denylist sets with a map keyed by contract address and updates parsing, selector logic, plugin/factory wiring, and tests; also changes TransactionEventFilter to match by address and topics.
> 
> - **Transaction selection logic**:
>   - Switch `deniedEvents` and `deniedBundleEvents` from `Set<TransactionEventFilter>` to `Map<Address, Set<TransactionEventFilter>>` in `LineaTransactionSelector`, `LineaTransactionSelectorFactory`, and `LineaTransactionSelectorPlugin`.
>   - Update `TransactionEventSelector` to lookup filters by `Address`, convert log topics to `Bytes32`-wrapped `LogTopic`s, and validate via the new matcher.
> - **Parsing/configuration**:
>   - `LineaTransactionSelectorCliOptions.parseTransactionEventDenyList` now returns `Map<Address, Set<TransactionEventFilter>>`, groups filters by address, and parses topics as fixed-size `Bytes32`.
>   - `LineaTransactionSelectorConfiguration` fields `eventsDenyList` and `eventsBundleDenyList` changed to `Map<Address, Set<TransactionEventFilter>>`.
> - **API change**:
>   - `TransactionEventFilter.matches` now accepts `Address` and varargs `LogTopic` instead of a `Log`.
> - **Tests**:
>   - Update tests to reflect map-based denylist and new matcher signature across selector and filter unit tests.
>

## Summary
Fix diagram control panel positioning and interaction issues in the VSCode extension preview.

### 1. Disable Gesture Zoom (892ab8e)
- Disable `mouseWheelZoomEnabled` to prevent unwanted trackpad gesture zoom
- Keep double-click zoom enabled for quick zoom functionality
- Maintain pan functionality with left mouse button drag

- Hide non-fullscreen diagrams when one diagram is in fullscreen mode

author: juliaregistrator
body:
- Registering package: EvoTrees
- Repository: https://github.com/Evovest/EvoTrees.jl
- Created by: @jeremiedb
- Version: v0.18.0
- Commit: 3534bd5f349fb356f8e790305166fb2ac429ec6f
- Reviewed by: @jeremiedb
- Reference: https://github.com/Evovest/EvoTrees.jl/commit/3534bd5f349fb356f8e790305166fb2ac429ec6f#commitcomment-168864696
- Description: Boosted trees in Julia
- Release notes:
<!-- BEGIN RELEASE NOTES -->
`````
## Refactor of GPU training backend
- Computations are now alsmost entirely done through `KernelAbstractions.jl`. Objective is to eventually have full support for AMD / ROCm in addition to current NVIDIA / CUDA devices.
- Important performance increase, notably for larger max depth. Training time is now closely increase linearly with depth. 

### Breaking change: improved reproducibility
- Training returns exactly the same fitted  model for a given learner (ex: `EvoTreeRegressor`). 
- Reproducibility is respected for both `cpu` and `gpu`. However, thes result may differ between `cpu` and `gpu`. Ie: reproducibility is guaranteed only within the same device type.
- The learner / model constructor (ex: `EvoTreeRegressor`) now has a `seed::Int` argument to set the random seed. Legacy `rng` kwarg will now be ignored.
- The internal random generator is now `Xishiro` (was previously `MersenneTwister` with `rng::Int`).

### Added node weight information in fitted trees 
- The train weight reaching each of the split/leaf nodes is now stored in the fitted trees. This is accessible via `model.trees[i].w` for the i-th tree in the fitted model. This is notably inteded to support SHAP value computations.
`````
<!-- END RELEASE NOTES -->
